section_summary: This section comprises diplomatic telegrams, despatches, letters, and transmittal memoranda from the American Embassy in Tokyo and the Japanese Embassy in Washington between January 1930 and March 1937 relating to the Japanese Imperial Diet. The documentation focuses on parliamentary proceedings, Cabinet decisions on Diet dissolution, and ministerial policy addresses delivered by Prime Minister Osachi Hamaguchi, Foreign Minister Kijuro Shidehara, and Finance Minister Junnosuke Inoue during the 57th, 58th, and 59th Diet sessions. Key topics include the lifting of the gold embargo, fiscal retrenchment, negotiations surrounding the London Naval Treaty of 1930, Sino-Japanese relations regarding customs autonomy and anti-bandit operations, and a March 1937 dissolution of the Lower House amidst rising military influence.

subfiles.about: Reporting the Japanese Government's dissolution of the Lower House of the Diet and the scheduling of a general election for April 30, 1937.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the Lower House was dissolved March 30, 1937 with an election April 30; major bills failed. The dissolution shows the Government avoiding party bickering and hoping for an army-led party.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 101 from Tokyo Regarding Dissolution of the Lower House

subfiles.about: Notifying the State Department of the Cabinet's decision to dissolve the Diet and the forwarding of Foreign Minister Shidehara's address.
subfiles.summary: Castle reports Shidehara's Diet address was sent to the Embassy in Washington and that the Cabinet decided privately to dissolve the Diet.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 7 from Tokyo Regarding Foreign Minister's Speech and Diet Dissolution

subfiles.about: Reporting the dissolution of the Imperial Diet on January 21, 1930, and the ordering of new general elections for February 20.
subfiles.summary: Castle reports the Diet was dissolved January 21, 1930 with an election February 20; the Hamaguchi government judged its chances favorable.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 8 from Tokyo Regarding the Formal Dissolution of the Diet

subfiles.about: Transmitting and summarizing the policy speeches delivered by Foreign Minister Shidehara, Premier Hamaguchi, and Finance Minister Inouye before the 57th Diet.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Castle transmits translated summaries and full press clippings of the addresses delivered before the Lower House of the Diet on January 21, 1930, by Baron Shidehara, Premier Hamaguchi, and Finance Minister Inouye. The despatch analyzes Shidehara's statements on Sino-Japanese relations, extraterritoriality, the Sino-Soviet Chinese Eastern Railway dispute, and the London Naval Conference, as well as Hamaguchi's plans regarding disarmament and domestic reforms. Transmitted newspaper clippings from The Japan Advertiser and The Japan Chronicle detail Hamaguchi's address and Inouye's comprehensive review of fiscal retrenchment, the lifting of the gold embargo, local tax reductions, and national debt management.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1 from Tokyo Transmitting Ministerial Addresses Before the 57th Diet

subfiles.about: Transmitting copies of Foreign Minister Shidehara's address before the special session of the Diet to Under Secretary Cotton.
subfiles.summary: Transmittal slip sending Under Secretary Cotton copies of Shidehara's Diet address.
subfiles.title: Transmittal Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs to Under Secretary Cotton

subfiles.about: Transmitting advance copies of Foreign Minister Shidehara's address before the special session of the Diet regarding the London Naval Treaty and China policy.
subfiles.summary: Second Secretary Kosaku Mizusawa, under the direction of Ambassador Katsuji Debuchi, transmits two advance copies of Foreign Minister Baron Shidehara's speech to be delivered before the special session of the Diet on April 25, 1930, requesting that one copy be provided to the Acting Secretary of State. The accompanying text outlines the conclusion of the Sino-Japanese customs agreement recognizing China's tariff autonomy on a reciprocal basis, while cautioning against anti-Japanese press reports. It further details the successful conclusion of the London Naval Treaty signed on April 22, defending Japan's cruiser and submarine tonnage allocations and arguing that the agreement adequately secures national defense while terminating costly naval building races.
subfiles.title: Letter from Japanese Embassy Transmitting Advance Text of Foreign Minister Shidehara's Diet Address

subfiles.about: Acknowledging receipt of advance copies of Baron Shidehara's Diet address and confirming transmittal of one copy to the Acting Secretary of State.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks Second Secretary Mizusawa for the Embassy's courtesy, confirming a copy of Shidehara's Diet address went to the Acting Secretary.
subfiles.title: Letter from Division of Far Eastern Affairs Acknowledging Receipt of Foreign Minister Shidehara's Speech

subfiles.about: Transmitting and reviewing the addresses delivered by Baron Shidehara, Premier Hamaguchi, and Finance Minister Inouye before the 58th Diet.
subfiles.summary: Counselor of Embassy Edwin L. Neville transmits translated newspaper clippings of addresses delivered by Baron Shidehara, Premier Hamaguchi, and Finance Minister Inouye before the 58th Extraordinary Session of the Diet on April 25, 1930. Neville summarizes the speeches and reviews domestic press criticism, noting editorial dissatisfaction with the government's economic vagueness and failure to offer substantive solutions for rising unemployment. Enclosed clippings from The Japan Advertiser contain the full published translations of Shidehara's defense of the London Naval Treaty and the Sino-Japanese customs accord, Hamaguchi's brief policy statement on the working budget and educational subsidies, and Inouye's survey of specie shipments and financial stabilization following the return to the gold standard.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 121 from Tokyo Transmitting Ministerial Addresses Before the 58th Diet

subfiles.about: Summarizing Foreign Minister Shidehara's upcoming annual address to the Diet regarding the London Naval Treaty, China, and U.S. immigration laws.
subfiles.summary: Forbes summarizes Shidehara's January 22, 1931 address: London Treaty's stabilizing effect, moderate China policy, fishing rights, and growing American understanding of Japan on the 1924 immigration law.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 9 from Tokyo Summarizing Foreign Minister Shidehara's Annual Address

subfiles.about: Transmitting the published text of Baron Shidehara's address before the Diet as Foreign Minister and Acting Premier.
subfiles.summary: Forbes sends the Japan Chronicle translation of Shidehara's January 22, 1931 address: London Treaty, naval building, protection of nationals in China, Manchurian railway disputes and measures against unemployment.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 127 from Tokyo Transmitting Foreign Minister Shidehara's Address to the Diet
